title: Rio Bravo onion (Rio Bravo F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Rio Bravo onion is an F1 hybrid onion variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Rio Bravo onion is an F1 hybrid onion variety, also sold or known as Rio Bravo F1 or Nunhems Rio Bravo. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Nunhems, sold by Allied Botanical.

heroImage.alt: Onion plants in beds separated by grassy paths on a Philippine farm, the kind of farm where Rio Bravo onion is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Rio Bravo F1 or Nunhems Rio Bravo, this is the same onion. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [onion variety finder](/crop-varieties/onion), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for onion and garlic](/land-preparation/onion-garlic-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit onion fields most often: [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [onion armyworm](/pests/onion-armyworm), [purple blotch of onion](/diseases/purple-blotch), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 65 to 70 days after transplanting (seller), matures about a week ahead of other Granex onions.
**Yield:** About 25 t/ha reported by Nueva Ecija growers, one Bongabon farmer got just under 24 t from 1.3 ha sown directly.
**Fruit:** Yellow Granex type: golden straw skin, uniform heavy bulbs of 90 to 100 g, sweet, fine neck, small root plate.
**Season:** Dry season, also sown off season from September.
Intermediate resistance to leaf miner, damping off, Alternaria blight, purple blotch, neck rot and bulb rot (seller's claim).
Used for off season September to October sowings in Nueva Ecija.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: Agriculture Monthly called it the dominant yellow onion in Nueva Ecija at about 25 t/ha, a 510 g Rio Bravo bulb won the yellow onion class at the 2015 Bongabon Sibuyas Festival. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual onion on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Rio Bravo onion

Red onion stores longer, while yellow onion yields more. Pick a variety that bulbs in the short days of the Philippine dry season, and plant it after the rains so the bulbs dry well. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Rio Bravo F1 the same as Rio Bravo?
items.a: Yes. Rio Bravo F1 is another name for Rio Bravo. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Rio Bravo?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
